checkpoints.description: Task 'muse-refine-loop' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan batch mode: schema-checked JSON manifest, per-track compose with attempts, progress and JSON summary, failing-first tests

impact_assessment.why: A project soundtrack is a set of themes, but muse renders one track per command; running the CLI by hand loses the set-level result and makes automation repeat flags and error handling
impact_assessment.benefits: One manifest renders and judges every track, reuses the refine loop per track, and returns a single exit code and machine-readable summary
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new batch command and manifest format; dependency: none added; concurrency: none, tracks render sequentially; state: one artifact folder per take per track
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reject unknown keys and cap the manifest at 50 tracks, default attempts=1, keep the existing per-track evidence and atomic writes, failing-first tests for parsing and exits

checkpoints.description: Task 'muse-batch-mode' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan resumable batch: per-track state written after every take, --resume reuses accepted tracks, --keep-going isolates failures, failing-first tests

impact_assessment.why: Batch mode stops on the first provider or judge failure, and rerunning the manifest re-renders and re-bills tracks that already succeeded
impact_assessment.benefits: A failed soundtrack run resumes at the first unfinished track, accepted evidence is reused, and one bad track no longer hides the rest of the set
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --resume/--keep-going flags and a hidden batch state file; dependency: none added; concurrency: one sequential writer; state: output/.muse-batch-<hash>.json updated atomically per track
impact_assessment.mitigation: Hash the validated manifest so a changed manifest refuses resume, skip only accepted tracks, write state after each track, keep default stop-on-failure behavior without --keep-going, failing-first tests

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Phase 4 gates 4/4; 109 offline tests; dogfood: state written, resume reused 3/3, missing evidence rerendered, keep-going recorded 0/3 failures then resumed to 3/3; checklists: passed

handoff.next: stage and commit the resumable batch feature
handoff.evidence: check 4/4, get batch state schema 1, reused/failed JSON verified

checkpoints.description: Task 'muse-batch-resume' completed successfully.
[1/5] Audit source, tests and packaging for correctness gaps; prioritize crash-safety, input validation, bounded reads and static findings

impact_assessment.why: The feature work is complete but the project has not had a full defect audit; a push should ship verified code, not just passing happy-path tests
impact_assessment.benefits: Crash-safe artifact writes, clear validation for library callers, bounded manifest reads and a clean static check reduce silent corruption and traceback paths
impact_assessment.risks: contract: input validation may reject previously accepted library values; dependency: none added; concurrency: none; state: artifact writes become stricter
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for every behaviour change, keep valid inputs unchanged, run all 4 gates and dogfood before pushing

checkpoints.description: Task 'muse-hardening-pass' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan round two: clean OSError boundary, trimmed/expanded env values, normalized Verdict sequences, malformed Gemini replies, and batch --dry-run with tests

impact_assessment.why: The first audit hardened storage and provider paths, but the CLI still tracebacks on raw OSError, env whitespace breaks names, Verdict accepts malformed sequences, Gemini assumes an object reply, and batch has no way to inspect a paid plan without spending
impact_assessment.benefits: Every filesystem failure is a clean 1 exit, environment values are forgiving, judge evidence is always well-typed, malformed replies fail with What/Why/Fix, and dry-run validates a manifest with zero provider calls
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --dry-run flag and stricter Verdict/strip behaviour; dependency: none added; concurrency: none; state: dry-run writes no artifacts or state
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for every branch, keep valid inputs unchanged, no provider or filesystem writes in dry-run, full gates before commit

checkpoints.description: [4/4] Round two complete: 144 tests, 4/4 gates; clean OSError exit, trimmed/expanded env, normalized Verdict sequences, malformed Gemini replies, batch --dry-run dogfooded with zero calls; checklists: passed

handoff.evidence: 144 tests OK, dry-run human/JSON exit 0 with no output/state, check 4/4

checkpoints.description: Task 'muse-audit-round2' completed successfully.
[1/5] Plan a read-only artifact catalog: scan muse.json evidence, filter/limit/JSON output, plus a monotonic Replicate poll deadline; failing-first tests

impact_assessment.why: Finished tracks are only discoverable by walking output folders, and Replicate's poll_timeout is an attempt count that ignores request latency, so both review and time budgets are weaker than documented
impact_assessment.benefits: One command lists scored evidence without provider calls, and a real deadline stops polling when the configured wall-clock budget is spent
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new list command and catalog fields; dependency: none added; concurrency: read-only scan; state: corrupt or oversized metadata is skipped with a warning
impact_assessment.mitigation: Read metadata with a size cap, validate schema fields, warn instead of traceback, keep list read-only, and inject a clock for deadline tests

checkpoints.description: [5/5] Catalog and deadline round complete: 155 tests, 4/4 gates; muse list human/JSON/filter/limit dogfooded, corrupt metadata warned, Replicate slow-poll deadline tested; checklists: passed

checkpoints.description: Task 'muse-catalog' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan judge preflight: build the required judge before rendering, keep --allow-unjudged lazy, prove the provider is never called when the judge key is missing

impact_assessment.why: compose builds the judge only after the provider renders, so a missing GEMINI_API_KEY wastes a paid render and leaves an unjudged artifact before failing
impact_assessment.benefits: Configuration errors stop before any provider call, while --allow-unjudged still renders and records judge_error exactly as documented
impact_assessment.risks: contract: required judge construction moves earlier; dependency: none added; concurrency: none; state: failed preflight leaves no artifact folder
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first provider-call counter test, explicit allow-unjudged regression test, full gates and CLI dogfood before push
